settings.title: Settings
settings.accentHelp: Every colour is adjusted until text on it stays readable.
settings.opacityHelp: How solid the window’s panels are. The working pane lands on this number; the columns beside it stay as much thinner as they were designed to be. Menus and sheets are solid, so they are not affected.
settings.languageHelp: Follow the system, or pick one.
settings.maxRowsHelp: Larger results are truncated rather than held in memory.
settings.keyboardHelp: Shortcuts are defined as data, so they are already overridable — the editor for changing them is not built yet.
settings.keyboardEdit: Click a shortcut to record a new one. Escape leaves it as it was.
settings.appearanceDesc: How the window is coloured and how much fits on screen. Every control here applies as you touch it.
settings.dataDesc: What a result brings back, and how you change what is in it.
settings.editorDesc: The SQL editor: how it is set, and what it does with a long line.
settings.fileDesc: Every preference on this page, as one document you can keep or carry to another machine.
settings.resetDesc: Puts every setting back to the way the app ships: appearance, data, the editor and the keyboard shortcuts.
settings.resetConfirm: Press again to put every setting back to its default.
settings.wasReset: Every setting is back to its default.
settings.exportRow: Write every preference to a file
settings.copyHint: Copy the whole document to the clipboard
settings.syntaxHelp: The editor, the chat and this JSON view.
settings.syntaxSync: Use one scheme for both appearances
settings.syntaxPreview: A sample of this scheme, light above dark

storage.title: Stored data
storage.where: Everything Shelf keeps is in one folder it owns:
storage.historyNote: Every statement run, with how long it took.
storage.chatsNote: Saved chats, including the rows the assistant read.
storage.jobsNote: The spooled rows of dispatched queries. Usually the largest.
storage.workspaceNote: Open tabs and the column widths of every grid.
storage.statsNote: Readings of the server's own counters, which the charts difference.
storage.savedNote: Queries you named and kept, and their earlier versions.
storage.providersNote: Configured providers and their API keys.
storage.connectionsNote: Every saved connection, its folders and its passwords.
storage.secretsGo: Passwords and API keys go with them. They are encrypted, but they are in this folder — the keyring holds only the key that opens them.
storage.notPreferences: Preferences are not touched. Reset them on the settings page.
storage.row: What this app keeps on this machine

update.sectionDesc: Where new versions come from, and when Shelf goes looking for one.
update.checkRow: Look for a newer version now
update.manualHint: This copy of Shelf was installed by something else — a package manager, or by hand — so the new version is downloaded from its page.
update.readyHint: Restarting takes a moment. Left alone, the update is applied the next time you quit.

host.unavailable: The process that opens databases could not be started. Restart Shelf to try again.

analyze.deadRows: The darker part of each bar is space held by dead rows.
analyze.unusedHint: Each one still costs a write on every insert and update.
analyze.brushHint: Drag across the chart to narrow everything below to that span.
analyze.noReadings: No readings yet. Shelf takes one when this panel is open, and differences them — leave it open and this fills in.
analyze.quietSelection: Nothing ran in the span you selected.

analyzeCaveat.short: The recorded history is shorter than this range, so this is everything since the first reading.
analyzeCaveat.cumulative: This is the server’s running total, not a range — leave this tab open and ranges will fill in.
analyzeCaveat.reset: The server reset its counters inside this range, so earlier readings were discarded.
analyzeCaveat.wide: Nothing was recorded between the readings either side of this range, so the nearest one available is older than the range asks for and this covers more than it says.

analyzeProblem.unsupported: This engine does not keep statement statistics.
analyzeProblem.not-installed: The statistics extension is not installed on this server.
analyzeProblem.not-permitted: This account cannot read the statistics view.
analyzeProblem.hint: On PostgreSQL, add the library to the server configuration, restart, then create the extension:
analyzeProblem.not-loaded: The extension is created but was never loaded, so it has counted nothing.
analyzeProblem.not-tracking: Statement recording is switched off on this server.
analyzeProblem.other-database: Statements are recorded on this server, but none for this database.
analyzeProblem.nothing-recorded: The extension is recording and has nothing yet.

jobs.empty: Nothing dispatched yet. A dispatched statement runs on its own, keeps its whole answer on this machine, and tells you when it is done.
jobs.rowsGone: This job no longer has its rows.
jobs.noMatches: No job matches what you are asking for.
jobs.nameHelp: How this run is listed under the jobs panel once it is away.

erd.nothing: There is nothing to diagram yet.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.settingsDesc: Model providers the assistant can use. Keys are encrypted with a key from the system keyring.
assistant.providersNote: Add a provider to turn a description into SQL. It is sent your table and column definitions, and it may run read-only queries — never anything that writes.
assistant.nameHelp: Optional. Left blank it is called after its provider.
assistant.modelHelp: Any model name this provider offers. The list is a starting point, not a limit.
assistant.baseUrlHelp: Leave blank for the provider's own. Set it for a local server or a gateway.
assistant.regionHelp: The AWS region the models are enabled in — us-east-1, eu-west-1. Requests are signed for it, so a wrong one is refused.
assistant.resourceHelp: Your resource's own endpoint — https://NAME.openai.azure.com. Required: an Azure resource is per-account, so there is no default.
assistant.deploymentHelp: The name your resource gave the model, not the model's own name.
assistant.credentialsCli: This program signs itself in. Shelf never reads or stores its credentials.
assistant.credentialsAws: Signed with the AWS credentials this machine already has — the environment, a profile, or an SSO session. Shelf never reads or stores them.
assistant.keyHelp: Encrypted with a key from the system keyring and kept in Shelf's own database. Sent from the background process, never from this window.
assistant.keyOptional: Optional. A local server usually needs none.
assistant.openingNote: The assistant can see {{scope}}. It reads, and it may run a query to check an answer. It never writes: anything that would change the database comes back as a statement for you to run yourself.
assistant.suggestCount: How many rows are in each table?
assistant.suggestJoin: How do these tables relate to each other?
assistant.signInWhy: {{name}} runs on this machine and holds its own account — Shelf never reads or stores its credentials. Nobody is signed in to it, so it has to be done in a terminal.
assistant.signInRun: Run this in a terminal, then check again.
assistant.signInStill: {{name}} still reports that nobody is signed in.
assistant.signInUnknown: Could not tell. Ask again and see what it says.
assistant.placeholder: Ask about the data, or describe a query
assistant.readsOnly: The assistant only runs queries that read. Anything that writes comes back for you to run.
assistant.cutOff: cut off at the row limit
assistant.notInstalledHelp: Not on this machine — install one and it appears here
assistant.fileRefused: Could not attach {{names}} — this provider reads text files, and images only where it says so.
